findings: Six of ten internal rejected crops produce checked editable masks. Crop rejection prevents otherwise possible fitting, but this does not show all six are correct crops.
Flower-cap and flame-cap examples have roughly plausible overlap proposals despite outer shapes outside the semicircular-lobe model. Framed bird also yields a recognizable motif.

The small checker is a counterexample to selecting crops by downstream fit: an undersized crop passes at 0.77% error. The crossed-bird example similarly passes while cutting through source decoration.
The remaining four separate into fine-checker image/paper failure and three feature-retention failures: Santa, foil leaf and swan. Geometry passes for all ten outputs.

Do not weaken crop gates globally or hide source-feature warnings. Next priority is independent overlap evidence using the visible lower edges, notch/diameter transitions and full photographed paper coverage, plus ink/reflectance-aware material estimates.
